deployed_ingest_probe: POST of an unsigned synthetic payload to the live endpoint returned HTTP 200 and stored the body with no processing enqueued, which is the CR-3 rule for an environment whose PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID is unset. Render still has no webhook id; the owner sets it.

listener.note_on_the_previous_attempt: The owner first registered the same URL with the dashboard wildcard '*' (all events). PayPal's webhook PATCH endpoint rejected every documented patch shape (415 then INVALID_WEBHOOK_PATCH_REQUEST), so the listener was deleted by the owner and re-registered through the API with the seven explicit types. The id changed to the one above, which is now in .env.
listener.registration: POST /v1/notifications/webhooks -> HTTP 201; GET by id -> HTTP 200 with exactly the seven types and no wildcard

outstanding_for_a_full_real_lifecycle: the four types above need the Phase 4-5 authorize/capture/void handlers, or a hand-run sandbox lifecycle with a buyer login
PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID=9WV04847640439813 in the Render env group before the deployed ingest can verify anything

scope_of_this_pass: S5 is a spike: its acceptance is to register the listener and record what the Sandbox actually does, per event type, including what cannot be produced. That is now done with executed evidence. It is NOT a claim that a real money lifecycle was verified today, and it does not enable webhook processing.

signature_verification.comparison: sending webhook_event as the raw body string instead returns HTTP 400 INVALID_REQUEST, so the shape in gateway.verify_webhook is the correct one and is now proven against a real PayPal-signed transmission
signature_verification.delivery: arrived after 33s with all five PayPal-Auth-* headers, 1716-byte body
signature_verification.false_start_recorded: an earlier run returned 400 INVALID_REQUEST because the request body was built with hyphenated keys (auth-algo) instead of the snake_case names PayPal expects. That was the probe's bug, not the product's, and is written down so nobody reads it as a PayPal limitation.
signature_verification.limitation: P4 and spikes.md classify simulator events as mock: this proves signature verification and the ingest plumbing, not a real capture lifecycle. The temporary listener was deleted and the tunnel stopped; nothing was left registered.
signature_verification.method: cloudflared quick tunnel to a local listener, POST /v1/notifications/simulate-event for PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED, then POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature built exactly as adapters/paypal/gateway.py verify_webhook builds it
signature_verification.result: HTTP 200 verification_status=SUCCESS with the production parsed-object shape

webhooks_enabled: false, deliberately. T03A03's acceptance says set it true when the handler ships; Phase 3 registers no money-state handler, so enabling it would advertise a processing path that does not exist. Recorded as the answer to that acceptance item rather than as a value to flip.
